intro: Ways to see the lakebed, mountains and farmland that shape Mexico City, on foot, by bike, by train and with the people who look after them.
policy: No link here earns Threadlands money. If that ever changes, those links will be labelled, and they will never change how a place is described or scored.

items.name: Muévete en Bici
items.what: Every Sunday from 8:00 to 14:00, about 55 to 60 km of streets, including Paseo de la Reforma, close to cars. Join anywhere along the route. Free bike and helmet loans and riding lessons at a few points, including Utopía Meyehualco in Iztapalapa.
items.how: Free. Routes change for some events, so check before you go.

items.name: Ecobici
items.what: The city's bike share: about 9,000 bikes, with plans to reach 15,000 and expand to Iztapalapa, Iztacalco and Tlalpan. Rides are up to 45 minutes each.
items.how: 1-day pass 134 pesos, 3 days 263, 7 days 441. Sign up online or in the app with an ID and a Visa or Mastercard.

items.name: Metro, Metrobús, Cablebús and trains
items.what: One card, the Tarjeta de Movilidad Integrada, pays for the Metro, Metrobús, Cablebús, Ecobici and the commuter trains below.
items.how: Buy and top it up at Metro stations.

items.name: Tren El Insurgente to Toluca
items.what: Fully open since February 2026, from Observatorio to Zinacantepec in the Toluca Valley in 40 to 50 minutes, crossing the forested sierra between the two basins. Observatorio connects with Metro lines 1 and 12 and the western bus terminal.
items.how: 100 pesos end to end, less for shorter trips. Daily from early morning to midnight.

items.name: Tren Suburbano to AIFA airport
items.what: Since April 2026 the commuter train runs from Buenavista to the Felipe Ángeles airport (AIFA) in about an hour, across the northern lakebed.
items.how: 45 pesos promotional fare with the city card.

items.name: Intercity coaches
items.what: Coaches leave from four terminals. Norte serves Teotihuacán and the north, Taxqueña (Sur) serves Cuernavaca and Morelos, TAPO serves Puebla and the east, and Observatorio (Poniente) serves Toluca and the west.
items.how: Buy at the terminal or from the bus companies.

items.name: Rutas del Campo
items.what: Farm visits run by producers on the city's conservation land in Xochimilco, Tláhuac, Tlalpan, Magdalena Contreras and Milpa Alta: beekeeping families, chinampa farms, cheese, honey and edible flowers. The city environment ministry (SEDEMA) runs the program so the income goes to the producers.
items.how: Book dates and prices at turismodenaturalezacdmx.com.

items.name: Arca Tierra in Xochimilco
items.what: A regenerative chinampa farm. A short trajinera ride from the Cuemanco pier, a walk through the fields with a farmer, then a meal from the harvest.
items.how: Limited dates. See their events page.

items.name: Michmani, Cuemanco
items.what: An eco-park on the Xochimilco canals with an axolotl refuge, canal and kayak tours, working chinampas and trails.
items.how: Daily 7:00 to 19:00, next to the Cuemanco pier.

items.name: Los Dinamos and the Magdalena River
items.what: 2,429 hectares of forest in Magdalena Contreras, along the last free-flowing river in the city, with about 26 km of trails, climbing routes and old power-plant ruins.
items.how: Bring warm layers and carry out your trash.

items.name: Parque Ecológico Lago de Texcoco
items.what: Part of the old lake, restored as wetland and parkland where the airport was planned. Migratory birds fill the lagoons in winter.
items.how: See it in the projects above.

sections.title: Places to stay
sections.none: We don't list places to stay yet. We'll only add one with a clear reason, like being locally run or close to the trails and trains above.

items.name: Two airports
items.what: AICM, in the city, is on Metro line 5 and Metrobús line 4. AIFA, to the north, is on the Tren Suburbano from Buenavista.
items.how: Flying is often the only practical way here from far away. We don't book flights, and we don't claim any way of getting here is sustainable.
